name: Crypto.com Design System
summary: Recreate Crypto.com's navy-dark, metallic-Visa-card fintech aesthetic with electric blue CTAs and mono-numeral pricing in SwiftUI.
description: A deep-dive SwiftUI prompt for rebuilding Crypto.com's premium navy-and-metal visual language: the tiered brushed-metal Visa card, the two-blue brand/accent system, and the mono-numeral money discipline that runs through balances, prices and APR.

whatYouGet: Complete SwiftUI Color/Font token set covering Crypto.com's navy canvas, dual-blue brand/accent split, and tiered card-metal gradients
Ready-to-adapt component specs for the metallic Visa card, the floating center Trade tab, and the total-balance hero
A house-rules checklist that keeps money mono, market colors unbroken, and the card's physical weight intact
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS/SwiftUI engineer who specializes in recreating best-in-class consumer fintech design systems with pixel-accurate tokens, typography, and motion. You have deep experience shipping crypto and trading apps and understand why premium financial products lean on physical-object metaphors (metal cards, weighty shadows) to build trust.
</role>

<reference_data>
Extracted facts from Crypto.com's iOS design language (use exactly these values unless the project fields below override them):

Color roles (dark, default theme):
- Canvas: #03060F (cool near-black, never neutral gray)
- Surface 1 (cards/sheets): #0B1426
- Surface 3 (chips/inputs/pressed rows): #15263F
- Divider: #1C3354
- Brand Navy (decorative only — hero gradients, promo banners): #002D74 to #103F68
- Accent Blue (all interactive/clickable elements): #1199FA, pressed #0B7AD1, 12% tint #1199FA1F
- Market up/buy green: #00C08B; market down/sell red: #F6485D — these never invert across themes
- Card gold (embossed tier text, chip accents): #C8A24A
- Text: primary #F4F7FB, secondary #8DA0BD, tertiary #5B6E8C
- Card-metal gradients: Midnight Blue #1A1A1E→#2A2A30 (1% cashback tier), Ruby Steel #5A1020→#8A1830 (2%), Jade Green #0E3A30→#14564A (3%), Obsidian #0A0A0C→#26262C (5%, flagship)

Typography:
- UI sans: Manrope (SIL OFL), weight ladder 400/600/700/800 — screen titles 32pt/800, section titles 22pt/800, body 16pt/400, buttons 15pt/700
- Numeric mono: Roboto Mono (Apache 2.0) for every balance, price, %, APR and the card's PAN — always with tabular/monospaced digits
- Balance hero: 30pt/600 mono; list price: 15pt/600 mono; card PAN: 15pt/500 mono with 2pt tracking

Spacing & radius:
- 4pt base spacing unit (scale: 4/8/12/16/20/24/28/32/40); 20pt horizontal screen inset (deliberately generous, "premium" feel, not terminal-dense)
- Radius scale: 6pt subtle chips, 10pt inputs, 14pt content cards, 18pt hero cards (including the Visa card), 24pt sheets/modals, 500pt (full pill) on all primary/secondary buttons and segmented controls, 50% circle on coin icons and the floating Trade button

Distinctive named UI/interaction patterns:
1. Metallic Visa Card hero — 1.586:1 aspect, 18pt radius, tier-specific brushed-metal gradient, 8% white diagonal gloss sheen, embossed gold tier name, gold chip, mono masked PAN, italic bold VISA wordmark, heaviest shadow in the whole system (black 0.8 opacity, 30pt radius, 14pt y-offset) — tap triggers a 3D Y-axis flip to reveal CVV
2. Floating center "Trade" tab — a 44pt filled accent-blue circle lifted -6pt above the 5-tab bar with an accent-tinted glow shadow, the one non-flat navigation element
3. Total-balance hero — label + big mono balance + colored today's P&L line, with an eye-toggle that cross-dissolves the value to bullet dots over 200ms
4. Watchlist/price row — coin icon, symbol+name stack, right-aligned mono price + colored mono % change
5. Card-tier carousel — horizontal paged scroll of the four metal gradients with a subtle 0.94→1.0 focus scale
6. Quick-action circle row (Deposit/Send/Trade/Earn) — 46pt flat circles with accent glyphs beneath the balance hero
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Never let Brand Navy (#002D74/#103F68) become a tappable control's fill — it is strictly decorative (hero gradients, one promo banner); Accent Blue (#1199FA) owns every clickable surface. Mixing the two collapses Crypto.com's core brand/interaction distinction.
2. Every monetary figure — balance, price, %, APR, PAN — must render in Roboto Mono with tabular digits. A proportional font here breaks column alignment down the watchlist and misaligns the card's PAN grouping.
3. Keep the canvas cool-navy, not neutral gray: #03060F/#0B1426 must retain a visible blue cast. A true near-black grayscale reads as generic dark mode, not this brand.
4. The Visa card always carries its heaviest shadow in the system (black 0.8 opacity) — this is the one place elevation should look almost theatrical, because the card's "physical weight" is the actual brand asset.
5. Market green/red (#00C08B / #F6485D) must never invert, even in a light theme variant — colorblind and habit-formed traders rely on the fixed mapping.
6. Buttons are always full pills (500pt radius); cards run 14-18pt. Do not introduce small/sharp radii anywhere in this system — it signals "terminal," which is explicitly the competitor posture this brand avoids.
7. The floating center Trade action is mandatory in any 5-tab bar recreation — it is the app's navigational signature, not a decorative extra, and should carry its own accent-tinted glow shadow distinct from every other tab.
8. Gold (#C8A24A) is reserved for card-tier embossing and reward badges only — never substitute it for the Accent Blue on primary CTAs, and never render the embossed tier name in plain white.
9. Dynamic Type should scale titles/body/labels but must NOT scale card text (PAN/tier name), numeric mono columns, or tab labels — those are layout-critical and will break card geometry and column alignment if they resize.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name / product: [YOUR APP NAME]
- Primary financial function (e.g. spot trading, card rewards, staking dashboard): [PRIMARY FUNCTION]
- Card program details, if applicable (tiers, cashback %, network): [CARD PROGRAM DETAILS]
- Target iOS version / minimum deployment target: [IOS VERSION]
- Brand color deviations from Crypto.com's palette, if any: [COLOR DEVIATIONS OR "none — use as specified"]
- Screens to build first (e.g. Home balance + watchlist, card detail, Earn): [PRIORITY SCREENS]
- Light-mode requirement (yes/no — Crypto.com is dark-first): [LIGHT MODE Y/N]
- Any existing design tokens or component library to integrate with: [EXISTING TOKENS/LIBRARY]
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete `Color` and `Font` SwiftUI extension file implementing every token in <reference_data>, adapted to any deviations named in <the_project>.
2. A `VisaCard`-equivalent hero component (or the project's card-tier component) with the tier-gradient enum, gloss overlay, embossed tier label, mono PAN, and the specified heavy shadow — plus the 3D flip interaction wired to a `@State` boolean.
3. A total-balance (or equivalent primary metric) hero component with the eye-toggle cross-dissolve behavior.
4. A 5-tab bar implementation with the floating center action circle, its glow shadow, and correct active/inactive glyph + label states.
5. A watchlist/list-row component (or the project's equivalent primary list atom) with correctly tabular mono pricing and colored % change.
6. A short design-QA checklist mapped to the <house_rules> above so a reviewer can verify the build didn't drift (e.g. "confirm no small-radius buttons shipped," "confirm PAN/tier stayed fixed under Dynamic Type").
7. Notes on any place the target app's actual requirements (from <the_project>) forced a deliberate deviation from the reference system, and why.
</what_to_give_me>

name: eBay Design System
summary: Rebuild eBay's dense, browse-fast marketplace UI in SwiftUI, centered on the signature bid-vs-Buy-It-Now badge and red watch-heart.
description: A structured SwiftUI prompt for recreating eBay's utilitarian white-canvas catalog design: the four-color brand discipline, the listing card, and the buy-mechanic badge that is the app's single fastest triage signal.

whatYouGet: Full SwiftUI Color/Font tokens for eBay's white-canvas, four-brand-color-with-discipline palette
A working listing-card, buy-mechanic badge, and Time Left countdown component set
House rules that protect the bid/Buy-It-Now contrast and the red (not blue) watch-heart convention
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS/SwiftUI engineer specializing in high-density commerce and marketplace UIs. You have shipped catalog/browse apps at scale and understand the difference between a UI optimized for scanning velocity versus one optimized for editorial impact — and why a marketplace with billions of listings must default to the former.
</role>

<reference_data>
Extracted facts from eBay's iOS design language:

Color roles:
- Canvas: #FFFFFF (pure white, kept deliberately unTinted for scan speed)
- Surface (search field, grouped fills): #F7F7F7; Surface pressed: #EFEFEF; Divider: #E5E5E5
- Four-color brand mark, used with strict discipline, not decoratively: Blue #0064D2 (primary action/link/active tab, pressed #0050A8), Red #E53238 (urgency only: time-left countdown, watch-heart active, price-drop), Yellow #F5AF02 (rating stars, "Top Rated" highlight), Green #86B817 ("or Best Offer" accent, "Refurbished" chips)
- Text: primary #191919, secondary #707070, tertiary #9B9B9B
- Deeper non-brand error red for forms/checkout failure: #C7000B; free-shipping label green: #258635
- Dark-mode variant exists but the four brand colors stay pixel-identical across themes — they are treated as equity-locked

Typography:
- Face: Inter as the free substitute for the proprietary Market Sans, a neutral highly-legible grotesque
- Weight discipline: concentrated at 400/600/700 only — no thin, no black
- Card price: 17pt/700; hero detail price: 24pt/700; card title: 15pt/400 (2-line clamp); badge text: 12pt/700 uppercase; time-left: 13pt/700
- Negative tracking reserved for titles/prices only (max -0.4pt); body sits at 0pt tracking

Spacing & radius:
- 4pt base unit; 16pt standard horizontal margin; listing grid uses a 12pt gutter
- Radius scale: 4pt on buy-mechanic badges and condition tags (deliberately squarer/tag-like), 8pt on listing cards/photos/search bar, 16pt on sheets, 999pt (full pill) on CTAs and filter chips, 50% circle on watch-heart backing and avatars

Distinctive named UI/interaction patterns:
1. Bid-vs-Buy-It-Now badge — the app's single fastest triage signal: a blue "BUY IT NOW" tag (light-blue fill, blue text) versus a neutral black-on-gray "X BIDS" tag; the contrast between the two IS the information, and they are intentionally squarer (4pt radius) than the full-pill CTAs around them
2. "Time Left" countdown — reads as plain gray text until under 24 hours, then switches to urgent red, with tabular/monospaced seconds once under an hour so digits never jitter
3. Watch-heart — red when active, not the brand blue; a 260ms scale 1.0→1.2→1.0 bounce plus a success haptic on toggle
4. eBay multicolor wordmark — the four-letter mark (e red / B blue / a yellow / y green) is equity-locked: never recolored, never rearranged
5. Listing card — square 1:1 product photo, watch-heart top-right, title (2-line clamp), price, buy-mechanic badge, optional "or Best Offer" and "Free shipping" line, all in a tight scannable stack
6. Minimal shadow discipline — cards use only a 0.06-opacity shadow; the flatness is deliberate so a catalog of 1.9 billion listings feels fast rather than fussy
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Never let the Buy-It-Now badge and the auction/bid badge look visually similar — the blue-vs-neutral contrast is the entire point of the component; if a reviewer can't tell the two apart at a glance, the badge has failed its job.
2. Keep the watch-heart red, not blue, even though blue is the brand's primary interactive color — eBay's own system deliberately breaks its own color-role convention here, and reproducing it correctly (not "fixing" it to blue) is a correctness requirement, not a stylistic choice.
3. Buy-mechanic badges and condition tags stay at a 4pt radius — squarer than the 999pt-pill CTAs — because they are tags conveying state, not tappable buttons; pilling them blurs that distinction.
4. The four brand colors (blue/red/yellow/green) are equity-locked: never recolor or rearrange the wordmark, and never repurpose yellow or green as a generic accent outside their named roles (ratings, Best Offer).
5. Cap weights at 400/600/700 — no thin or light weights anywhere; eBay's density needs legibility, not delicacy.
6. Time Left must use tabular/monospaced digits once it drops into seconds-display mode (under 1 hour) so the countdown never visually jitters as digits change width.
7. Keep shadows minimal (around 0.06 opacity) on list-mode and grid cards — separation comes from whitespace and hairline dividers, not elevation; heavier shadows read as slow/fussy for this catalog-density use case.
8. Canvas stays pure white (#FFFFFF), never tinted — a neutral canvas keeps thousands of varied product photos color-accurate and avoids competing with brand-color badges.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name / product: [YOUR APP NAME]
- Marketplace category (general goods, auctions-only, fixed-price-only, etc.): [MARKETPLACE TYPE]
- Buy mechanics supported (Buy It Now / Auction / Best Offer — which combination): [BUY MECHANICS]
- Target iOS version / minimum deployment target: [IOS VERSION]
- Brand color deviations from eBay's four-color mark, if any: [COLOR DEVIATIONS OR "none — use as specified"]
- Screens to build first (e.g. browse grid, listing detail, watchlist): [PRIORITY SCREENS]
- Localization / non-Latin script requirements: [LOCALIZATION NEEDS]
- Any existing design tokens or component library to integrate with: [EXISTING TOKENS/LIBRARY]
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete `Color` and `Font` SwiftUI extension file implementing every token above, adjusted for any brand deviations named in <the_project>.
2. A `BuyMechanicBadge` component supporting both the Buy-It-Now and Auction/bid states with the correct visual contrast, plus an optional "Best Offer" append.
3. A `TimeLeft` countdown view with the 24-hour color threshold and tabular-digit sub-1-hour mode.
4. A `ListingCard` component (grid and list variants) assembling photo, watch-heart, title clamp, price, badge, and shipping/time-left meta.
5. A `WatchHeart` toggle component with the correct red-not-blue color and bounce animation.
6. A short QA checklist mapped to the house rules (e.g. "confirm badge contrast is unmistakable at a glance," "confirm watch-heart is red not blue").
7. Notes on any deliberate deviation the target app's actual buy mechanics (from <the_project>) required from the reference system.
</what_to_give_me>

name: Etsy Design System
summary: Recreate Etsy's warm handmade-marketplace look in SwiftUI, built around the cream canvas, the bouncing favorite-heart, and maker photography.
description: A detailed SwiftUI prompt for rebuilding Etsy's warm-cream, single-orange-accent commerce design — including the shop banner header and the near-black review stars that break from every other marketplace's gold-star convention.

whatYouGet: Full SwiftUI Color/Font tokens for Etsy's warm-cream canvas and single-orange-accent system
A handmade product-card, favorite-heart, and shop-banner-header component set
House rules protecting the cream canvas, near-black review stars, and warm-tinted card shadows
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS/SwiftUI engineer specializing in warm, editorial commerce interfaces for maker and craft marketplaces. You understand how a canvas's color temperature alone can signal "handmade" versus "mass-produced," and you're careful to preserve that signal rather than defaulting to the stark-white canvas most commerce apps use.
</role>

<reference_data>
Extracted facts from Etsy's iOS design language:

Color roles:
- Canvas Cream: #FAF5EF (the brand's signature warm-paper tone — never stark white)
- Card White: #FFFFFF (product cards float on the cream); Surface: #F1F1F1; Divider: #E1DDD5 (a warm, not neutral, gray)
- Etsy Orange: #F1641E, pressed #D5571A, tint #FDEDE4 — the single accent color, reserved structurally (action/active/sale/favorite), never used as body text or decoration
- Text: primary #222222, secondary #595959, tertiary #8A8A8A
- Review stars are rendered near-black (#222222), a deliberate departure from the gold/yellow stars used by most competitors
- Sale/error red: #A61A12 (deep brick, used sparingly); success green: #258635
- Dark mode exists (warm dark canvas #1A1714) but Etsy Orange stays pixel-identical across themes

Typography:
- Face: Inter as the free substitute for the proprietary Graphik, a friendly slightly-editorial grotesque
- Weight discipline: 400/500/700 — medium (500) does the warm, human mid-emphasis work for shop names and maker copy, never shouty
- Listing hero title: 22pt/700; card title: 15pt/500 (2-line clamp); card price: 16pt/700; shop name: 14pt/500
- Negative tracking only on titles (max -0.4pt); body at 0pt for readability

Spacing & radius:
- 4pt base unit; 16pt standard horizontal margin, 24pt between sections; product grid uses a 12pt gutter
- Radius scale: 8pt on inline thumbnails/reviewer photos, 12pt on product cards/shop banner/sheets, 16pt on bottom sheets/modal cards, 999pt (full pill) on CTAs/filter chips/search bar/badges, 50% circle on favorite-heart backing and avatars

Distinctive named UI/interaction patterns:
1. Favorite heart — the emotional core of the app: outline idle, solid orange active, with a 300ms spring bounce that overshoots to roughly 1.25x scale plus a success haptic; sits on a dark circular backing when placed over photos
2. Handmade product card — full-width 1:1 maker photo, title/price/star-row/shop-name/shipping stack, an orange-tint "Bestseller" pill top-left when applicable
3. Shop banner header — a full-width maker banner image with a circular shop avatar (white ring) overlapping its bottom edge, shop name, sales count + rating, and a "Follow shop" outline pill
4. Warm-tinted card shadow — white cards cast a soft low-opacity brown-toned shadow (not neutral gray) so they read as prints resting on cream paper rather than floating in cold space
5. Listing image gallery — full-bleed paged maker-photo carousel with dot indicators and floating circular controls over the photo
6. Near-black review stars — a deliberate break from gold-star convention across the review row and rating summary
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Never replace the cream canvas (#FAF5EF) with stark white — the warmth is the single biggest differentiator from every other marketplace app; reproducing this system on pure white defeats its purpose entirely.
2. Etsy Orange is structural only — reserve it for the primary action, active tab, sale callouts, and the favorite heart. Never use it for body text, decorative accents, or a second brand color; the single-accent discipline is core to the identity.
3. Render review stars near-black (#222222), not gold/yellow — this is a specific, intentional departure from typical marketplace convention and should not be "corrected" back to gold.
4. Card shadows must be warm-tinted brown, not neutral gray — a cold gray shadow under a white card on cream canvas immediately reads as generic and breaks the "print on paper" effect this system relies on.
5. Always lead product cards and the listing detail with large, color-rich maker photography — the photo is the hero of every card; never shrink it to make room for text.
6. Keep the favorite-heart's bounce (spring overshoot to ~1.25x) and success haptic intact on every implementation — skipping the bounce loses the tactile, emotional signature the whole interaction is built around.
7. CTAs are always full-pill (999pt radius) and friendly — never introduce sharp or small-radius buttons, which would clash with the warm, human tone.
8. Keep shop names and maker copy at medium weight (500), not bold or regular — this is the specific weight Etsy uses to sound warm and human without shouting.
9. Do not introduce a second saturated accent color alongside orange — the single-orange-plus-cream palette is the entire identity; a second accent dilutes it.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name / product: [YOUR APP NAME]
- Marketplace category (handmade goods, vintage, art prints, etc.): [MARKETPLACE CATEGORY]
- Primary maker/seller-facing or buyer-facing focus: [MAKER OR BUYER FOCUS]
- Target iOS version / minimum deployment target: [IOS VERSION]
- Brand color deviations from Etsy's orange, if any: [COLOR DEVIATIONS OR "none — use as specified"]
- Screens to build first (e.g. browse grid, listing detail, shop page): [PRIORITY SCREENS]
- Photography guidelines / asset constraints: [PHOTO CONSTRAINTS]
- Any existing design tokens or component library to integrate with: [EXISTING TOKENS/LIBRARY]
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete `Color` and `Font` SwiftUI extension file implementing every token above, adjusted for any deviations named in <the_project>.
2. A `FavoriteHeart` component with the correct spring-bounce animation, success haptic, and dark circular photo-backing variant.
3. A `ProductCard` component assembling the maker photo, bestseller tag, title, price, near-black star row, and shop-name line.
4. A `ShopBannerHeader` component with the banner image, overlapping circular avatar, shop stats line, and "Follow shop" pill.
5. A warm-tinted card shadow modifier that can be applied consistently across all elevated surfaces.
6. A short QA checklist mapped to the house rules (e.g. "confirm canvas is cream not white," "confirm stars are near-black not gold").
7. Notes on any deliberate deviation the target app's actual marketplace category (from <the_project>) required from the reference system.
</what_to_give_me>

name: Fidelity Design System
summary: Rebuild Fidelity's calm, institutional brokerage UI in SwiftUI, anchored by tabular-figure discipline and a sacred green/red gain-loss rule.
description: A rigorous SwiftUI prompt for recreating Fidelity's quiet, data-first brokerage design system, where every dollar is tabular and green/red are reserved exclusively for financial semantics.

whatYouGet: Full SwiftUI Color/Font tokens for Fidelity's evergreen dark mode and disciplined gain/loss semantics
A balance-hero, sparkline-with-range-tabs, and sticky trade-button component set
House rules protecting the tabular-figure rule and the strict financial-only meaning of green/red
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS/SwiftUI engineer who specializes in institutional brokerage and trading-platform UI. You have built production trade-ticket flows and understand why a serious financial product must treat color and numeral alignment as functional signals rather than decoration — a misused semantic color in a brokerage app erodes trust in a way a marketing app never risks.
</role>

<reference_data>
Extracted facts from Fidelity's iOS design language:

Color roles:
- Canvas: #FFFFFF light / #0E1411 dark — the dark canvas is a deliberate deep evergreen, never pure black
- Surface Gray (light): #F4F6F4; Dark Surface 1: #16201B; Dark Surface 2: #1F2C24; Divider: #E1E5E1 light / #26342B dark
- Fidelity Green (brand/primary action): #368727, pressed #2A6B1F; Heritage Green (money-movement actions like Transfer): #00754A; Leaf accent (dark-mode links/selected): #4FB23B
- Financial semantics — the most protected rule in the system: Gain #15833E light / #15B374 dark; Loss #D32F2F light / #E5544B dark; Flat uses the secondary text color, never a third saturated color
- Text: primary #1A1F1B light / #E8EFE9 dark, secondary #5A655C light / #9DB0A2 dark
- Gold tier accent (premium/Private Client Group): #C8A24B; info link blue: #1E6FB8

Typography:
- Face: Inter as the free substitute for the proprietary "Average Sans"; tabular/lining figures mandatory everywhere money appears (balances, prices, %, $ deltas, table columns) — this numeral discipline is described as the single most recognizable typographic trait of the brand
- Balance hero: 34pt/800; screen title: 26pt/700; row value: 16pt/700 tabular; numeric mono line ($ delta + %): 13pt/600 tabular
- Restrained overall type scale (10pt to 34pt) — hierarchy comes from weight and tabular emphasis rather than dramatic size jumps

Spacing & radius:
- 4pt base unit; 20pt horizontal screen inset (16pt for full-bleed charts/cards); list rows target 64pt height with 12pt vertical padding
- Radius scale: 4pt inline chips/tags, 8pt buttons/inputs/search bar/performance pills, 12pt cards (account/quote/estimate), 16-20pt sheets/modals, 500pt pill on filter/range tabs/segmented toggles, 50% circle avatars

Distinctive named UI/interaction patterns:
1. Total account value as the screen hero — a 34pt/800 tabular numeral with a day-change line (triangle glyph + colored $ delta + % + "today") and a sparkline directly beneath, at the very top of Summary
2. Portfolio-to-quote drill path — Summary → Account → Position → Quote → Trade is the product's spine; every screen along it keeps the same calm chrome
3. Sparkline + range-tab pair — a 2pt colored stroke chart with a gradient fill, paired with compact 1D/1W/1M/1Y/5Y/All pill tabs directly beneath; tapping a range morphs the path over ~280ms
4. Sticky bottom Trade button — pinned to every quote screen with a translucent blurred backdrop and a top divider, never buried below the fold
5. Performance pill — a gain/loss/flat badge with a light-opacity tint background, a leading triangle glyph, and always-tabular numerals
6. Flat hairline-separated holdings list — cards are reserved only for account/quote/estimate groupings; plain list rows never get a card border or shadow
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Green and red are reserved exclusively for financial gain/loss semantics — never repurpose them for a generic destructive button, a generic success toast, or any non-financial state that could be mistaken for a price move. This is the single most important rule in the entire system.
2. Every monetary figure — balance, price, %, $ delta, quantity — uses tabular/monospaced lining figures. A proportional numeral anywhere money appears breaks column alignment and violates the brand's defining typographic trait.
3. The dark canvas is a deep evergreen (#0E1411), never pure black — a true black reads as generic dark mode and loses the brand's institutional-calm identity.
4. The total account value is always the visual hero of its screen — largest, boldest element (34pt/800), with its day-change line and sparkline directly beneath it; never let a marketing element or illustration compete with it.
5. The sticky Trade button must always be reachable — never let it scroll out of view or bury it below other content on a quote/trade screen.
6. Keep holdings and watchlist rows as flat, hairline-separated single-column lists; reserve cards exclusively for account summary, quote, and estimated-cost groupings. Wrapping every row in a card contradicts the system's restrained, data-first posture.
7. Never animate a changing balance with a sliding/rolling digit effect — only a brief (~600ms) color cross-fade on tick, then settle back to the primary text color. Money should never appear to "jump."
8. Do not introduce a second saturated accent color beyond the two greens — the palette is green (brand + semantic) plus near-greyscale everywhere else; a second accent dilutes the discipline that makes gain/loss legible at a glance.
9. Motion stays calm throughout: 120-300ms ease-out transitions, no bounce or spring effects applied to financial data — this is a brokerage, not a rewards app.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name / product: [YOUR APP NAME]
- Brokerage/finance function (self-directed trading, retirement planning, robo-advisor, etc.): [PRIMARY FUNCTION]
- Asset classes supported (equities, options, mutual funds, crypto): [ASSET CLASSES]
- Target iOS version / minimum deployment target: [IOS VERSION]
- Brand color deviations from Fidelity's greens, if any: [COLOR DEVIATIONS OR "none — use as specified"]
- Screens to build first (e.g. Summary, quote/chart, trade ticket): [PRIORITY SCREENS]
- Regulatory/compliance UI requirements (disclosures, order confirmations): [COMPLIANCE REQUIREMENTS]
- Any existing design tokens or component library to integrate with: [EXISTING TOKENS/LIBRARY]
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete `Color` and `Font` SwiftUI extension file implementing every token above, including a scheme-aware gain/loss resolver function, adjusted for any deviations named in <the_project>.
2. A `BalanceHeader` hero component with the day-change line and tabular numerals.
3. A `Sparkline` chart view paired with a range-tab row (1D/1W/1M/1Y/5Y/All) and the specified morph animation.
4. A `HoldingRow` list-item component and a sticky bottom `TradeBar` component with the correct blurred-backdrop treatment.
5. A `PerformancePill` component covering gain/loss/flat states.
6. A short QA checklist mapped to the house rules (e.g. "confirm no non-financial UI uses green/red," "confirm every money label is tabular").

name: Klarna Design System
summary: Recreate Klarna's soft pink-and-black BNPL interface in SwiftUI, centered on the four-dot Pay-in-4 schedule timeline.
description: A detailed SwiftUI prompt for rebuilding Klarna's calm, gliding "smooth" design language — the pink-with-near-black-text rule, the single dark hero anchor, and the literal four-dot payment-plan visualization.

whatYouGet: Full SwiftUI Color/Font tokens for Klarna's pink-and-near-black palette with soft pink surface wells
A Pay-in-4 schedule timeline, black payment-summary hero, and order-row component set
House rules protecting the near-black-on-pink contrast rule and the system's deliberately slow, gliding motion
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS/SwiftUI engineer who specializes in buy-now-pay-later and consumer fintech interfaces. You understand why Klarna's whole personality rests on two disciplines working together — a strict single-accent color rule and deliberately unhurried motion — and you know that breaking either one collapses the "smooth" brand promise into a generic pink theme.
</role>

<reference_data>
Extracted facts from Klarna's iOS design language:

Color roles:
- Canvas: #FFFFFF with a soft pink-tinted surface well #FFF2F5 for grouped content; Divider: #F0DDE3 (a warm pink-leaning gray); Border: #E2D2D8
- Klarna Pink: #FFB3C7, pressed #F49CB4 — the single action color, and it is ALWAYS paired with near-black text (#0B051D), never white text
- Black/near-black structural ink: #0B051D (has a violet cast, not pure black), hover state #1A1330 — used for headings, amounts, and the one dark hero panel in the whole system
- Text: primary #0B051D, secondary #6E6878, tertiary #9B96A3
- Semantic: success green #0E8A4F, upcoming-payment amber #A9700E, error red #C8102E
- Dark mode exists (#0B051D canvas) but Klarna Pink stays pixel-identical across themes and always keeps near-black text on its fills

Typography:
- Face: Klarna Text (proprietary humanist sans), Inter as free substitute; Klarna Display used for the largest hero amount
- Tabular figures mandatory in amounts, the Pay-in-4 schedule, and order totals
- Amount hero: 36pt/700; screen title: 28pt/700; plan amount: 22pt/700; body/title: 16pt/600
- Negative tracking only on large numbers/titles (-0.3 to -0.5pt); body sits at 0pt with a relaxed 1.5 line-height

Spacing & radius:
- 4pt base unit; 20pt standard screen margin (slightly roomier than most fintech systems for a calmer feel); 20-24pt card internal padding
- Radius scale runs notably soft: 12pt small chips/logos, 16pt inputs/tiles, 20pt cards/schedule-card/modules, 24pt the black hero and bottom-sheet top corners, 28pt primary CTAs (a very soft near-full pill), 50% circle quick-action circles/schedule dots/avatars

Distinctive named UI/interaction patterns:
1. Pay-in-4 schedule timeline — the signature object: four dated dots on a connecting track, the first filled pink with a near-black check ("paid"), the rest outlined (next = solid ring, upcoming = light ring), each labeled with a tabular date and amount; the whole BNPL proposition rendered as one calm, literal picture — never hidden behind a summary
2. Black payment-summary hero — the system's single dark anchor: a full-width near-black panel with an uppercase pink "TOTAL DUE" label, a large white tabular amount, and a pink "Pay now" affordance; no other panel in the app is allowed to go this dark
3. In-app shopping browser — Klarna wraps any merchant's store in its own chrome: a URL pill, a persistent pink "Pay with Klarna" footer bar, and a smooth slide-up checkout sheet, so shopping never visually leaves Klarna's frame
4. Order list rows — clean purchase-history rows with a merchant logo, plan summary, tabular amount, and a status pill (paid/upcoming/failed)
5. The soft pink CTA — a very-soft-radius (28pt) full-width pill button with near-black text, a slow ~160ms press-scale, and a soft haptic
6. Slide transitions — screens and sheets glide in over roughly 300-360ms, deliberately slower than typical iOS transitions, reinforcing the "smooth" brand word
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Never put white text on Klarna Pink — it fails contrast and is a fundamental brand violation; near-black (#0B051D) is the only text color that ever sits on a pink fill.
2. Do not introduce blue, a gradient, or any second accent color — pink plus near-black is the entire visual story; adding a second saturated color dilutes the calm, restrained identity.
3. Never hide the Pay-in-4 schedule behind a summary number — the four-dot timeline IS the product's core promise made visible, and it should be the most prominent module on any payment-plan screen.
4. Use near-black (#0B051D), not pure black, for all structural ink — it carries a violet cast that is specific to this brand and should not be flattened to true black.
5. Keep radii soft throughout — 28pt on primary CTAs, 20-24pt on cards — and never introduce a sharp or small-radius button; the unusually generous softness is a deliberate, load-bearing brand signal.
6. Only one panel in the entire app may go fully dark — the black payment-summary hero. Introducing a second dark panel dilutes its function as the system's single visual anchor.
7. Transitions must stay slow and gliding (roughly 300-360ms ease), never snap instantly — Klarna's whole personality is built on feeling unhurried; a fast, snappy transition reads as a different brand entirely.
8. Tabular figures are mandatory for every amount in the schedule, order totals, and plan lines so decimal points align down the column.
9. Never use light or thin font weights for amounts — Klarna's amount typography runs at weight 700 specifically to feel confident despite the soft, friendly palette around it.
</house_rules>

</the_project>

2. A `PayInFourCard` (or equivalent installment schedule) component with the paid/next/upcoming dot states and connecting track.

whatYouGet: Full SwiftUI Color/Font tokens for Monzo's coral-and-navy palette plus the Pot accent-color set
A coral card hero, transaction-row, and Pot-coin component set with correct gradients and shadows

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS/SwiftUI engineer who specializes in friendly, human-centered digital banking interfaces. You understand why Monzo deliberately trades dashboard density for a scrollable transaction feed, and why a single unmistakable brand color paired with a grounding neutral is more memorable than a broader palette.
</role>

<reference_data>
Extracted facts from Monzo's iOS design language:

Color roles:
- Hot Coral: #FF3464, pressed #E02855 — the brand color, identical in light and dark, used for the card hero, primary CTAs, active tab state, and key links
- Monzo Navy: #14233C — the grounding "trust" counterweight, used as light-mode ink and dark-mode card/row surface; Navy Deep #0E1620 is the dark canvas, one step darker, never pure black
- Canvas: #F6F7F9 light (a cool off-white, never pure white) / #0E1620 dark; Surface: #FFFFFF light / #14233C dark; Divider: #E4E7EB light / #243A57 dark
- Text: primary #14233C light / #F4F6F9 dark, secondary #5C6B82 light / #9FB0C6 dark
- Pot & category accent set (used for savings goals and transaction categories, stays fully saturated in both themes): Mint #2FB59A/#5CE0C4, Sky #3E7FC4/#5AA9F0, Gold #E0A23A/#FFC75F, Violet #7A4FD0/#A98AE6, Teal #1F9E8F/#46C7B7
- Semantic: income green #1FA971 light/#2FCB8F dark; error red #E0354A/#FF5A6E

Typography:
- Face: Inter throughout, chosen specifically for its strong tabular-figure legibility for balances
- Weight ladder: 400 body, 500-600 labels/merchant names, 700 section titles, 800 balance/screen titles — no thin, no italic anywhere
- Balance/hero number: 30pt/800 tabular; screen title: 32pt/800; merchant/row title: 15pt/600; amount: 15pt/700 tabular
- Tracking tightens as size grows: roughly -0.2pt at 18pt down to -0.6pt at 32pt

Spacing & radius:
- 4pt base unit; 20pt screen horizontal inset for card/feed/Pots; transaction rows use a 20pt inset with a 14pt icon-to-text gap
- Radius scale: 4pt progress-bar fills, 12pt inputs/search bar/Pot-coin inner square, 14pt buttons/secondary surfaces, 16-18pt cards/sheets/Pot coins, 500pt pill buttons/category chips, 50% circle merchant icons/avatars

Distinctive named UI/interaction patterns:
1. Hot Coral card hero — a full-width gradient card (coral through a lighter coral to a deeper pressed coral) at the very top of Home, ~132pt tall with an 18pt radius, carrying its own coral-tinted shadow; tapping it triggers a 3D Y-axis flip to reveal card controls
2. Transaction feed as the primary interface — day-grouped rows (TODAY/YESTERDAY/date headers with a day total), each row a circular merchant icon (real logo or a colored emoji fallback by category), merchant name, "category · time" meta line, and a right-aligned tabular amount; this feed replaces a conventional dashboard
3. Pots — round-cornered "coin" savings goals with gradient fills and a centered emoji, displayed as a horizontally-scrolling strip directly under the card hero; a "New pot" tile uses a dashed border
4. Big confident tabular numbers — the balance is always the largest type element on Home, reinforcing that money is the headline
5. Category emoji + tint system — every transaction category gets both an emoji glyph and a matching background tint at roughly 14-18% opacity
6. Flat surfaces with hairline dividers — gradients are reserved exclusively for the card hero and Pot coins; everything else (rows, list sections) stays flat with dividers, not boxes or shadows
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. The Hot Coral card must be the unmistakable hero at the top of Home, with clear margin and its own coral-tinted shadow — never replace it with a plain balance number or bury it below other content.
2. Ground every dark-mode surface in Monzo Navy (#14233C) and the darkest canvas in Navy Deep (#0E1620) — never substitute pure black; the navy cast is what keeps the coral feeling trustworthy rather than gimmicky.
3. Build the transaction list as a rich, tappable feed — merchant icon, category+time meta, amount — never as a dense spreadsheet-style table; the feed IS the interface, not a secondary view.
4. Never drop the circular merchant-icon/emoji-fallback treatment on transaction rows — the colorful category circles are core to the feel and should not be simplified to plain text rows.
5. Reserve gradients strictly for the card hero and the Pot coins; every other surface (rows, sections, sheets) stays flat with hairline dividers, never a second gradient surface.
6. The active tab state is coral icon fill plus coral label text only — never add a background tint pill behind the active tab icon.
7. Keep every amount tabular (`.monospacedDigit()`) so columns of money align — this applies to the balance, transaction amounts, and Pot totals alike.
8. Never desaturate Pot coins or category accent colors in dark mode — only chrome (dividers, secondary text) should dim; content colors stay fully saturated.
9. Weight discipline stays upright at 400-800 — no thin or italic Inter weights anywhere in the system.
</house_rules>

</the_project>

You understand why Nubank treats a single brand color as the entire identity rather than one accent among several, and why its Home screen is deliberately short rather than dashboard-dense.
</role>

<reference_data>
Extracted facts from Nubank's iOS design language:

Color roles:
- Nu Purple: #820AD1 — the identity itself, identical in light and dark mode, used for the full-bleed hero header, primary CTAs, and the Roxinho credit card; Purple Bright #9B2BE0 (gradient top/progress fill); Purple Pressed #6A07AD; Purple Soft #C9A6E8 (dark-mode interactive tint for active tab/secondary-button text)
- Canvas: #F4F2F7 light (a faint cool lilac-white, never pure white) / #15101C dark (a deep aubergine tinted from Nu Purple, never pure black); Surface: #FFFFFF light / #1F1729 dark; Divider: #E6E1EE light / #362B47 dark
- Text: primary #1A1523 light (near-black with an aubergine cast) / #F3EEF8 dark (a purple-tinted off-white); secondary #6B6178 light / #B6A8C8 dark
- Product accents: Positive green #1FB76A/#2ED47A, Investment gold #D9A227/#F5C24B, Highlight pink #D9469E/#E85FB0, Info blue #3D7AE0/#5A95F0
- Error red #E03A4A/#FF5C6C; warning amber #D9821F/#FFB347

Typography:
- Face: Inter as the free substitute for the proprietary Graphik/Nu Sans; tabular figures mandatory wherever currency appears
- Weight ladder: 400 body, 500 meta/labels, 600 row titles, 700 greeting/section headers, 800 balance/screen titles — no thin, no italic
- Balance/hero number: 26pt/800 tabular; screen title: 32pt/800; greeting/section: 22pt/700; row/tile title: 15pt/600
- Tracking tightens from roughly -0.2pt at 18pt down to -0.6pt at 32pt

Spacing & radius:
- 4pt base unit; 18-22pt screen inset (tiles at 18pt, rows/headers at 22pt); tile internal padding 18pt with a 14pt tile-to-tile vertical gap
- Radius scale: 4pt progress-bar fills, 8pt inline chips/mini credit-card icon, 12pt input fields, 14pt nested mini-tiles, 16pt account/credit tiles and cards, 24pt bottom-sheet top corners, 500pt (full pill) on every button/search bar/status chip, 50% circle avatars/quick-action circles

Distinctive named UI/interaction patterns:
1. Full-bleed purple hero header — a flat purple color block (or a subtle top-to-bottom gradient) filling the top of Home with avatar, greeting, and white chrome icons; deliberately never shadowed, since it's treated as a flat brand block rather than a floating card
2. Tile-based Home under "fewer, clearer choices" — the NuConta balance tile, quick-action shortcuts, credit-invoice tile, and activity feed are each a single clean rounded tile; the screen is intentionally kept short, with anything less common pushed one tap deeper rather than crowding the first screen
3. Roxinho credit tile — a small purple-gradient mini-card icon paired with the invoice total, due date, and a limit-used progress bar; tapping opens the full card screen
4. Quick-action shortcuts — circular buttons (Pix, Pagar, Cartões, Investir) in a horizontal strip directly under the balance tile, each with a stroke icon and a short caption
5. Pix-first money movement — Pix is treated as the primary, most prominent quick action, with an animated green-check success receipt on completion
6. Activity row — a circular icon, title, source+time meta, and a right-aligned tabular amount (green for income, primary-text color for spend), matching the pattern used across the tiles
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Nu Purple (#820AD1) is the entire brand identity, not one accent among several — never dilute it with a second saturated brand color, and keep it pixel-identical across light and dark themes.
2. The purple hero header must remain a flat color block with no shadow — it is intentionally not treated as a floating card; adding elevation to it breaks the "bold block, calm content" contrast that defines the Home screen.
3. Follow "fewer, clearer choices": keep Home intentionally short, surfacing only the balance tile, quick actions, credit tile, and recent activity — resist the urge to add dashboards, charts, or stacked promotional banners to the first screen.
4. Use deep aubergine (#15101C), not pure black, for the dark canvas — it must read as tinted from Nu Purple, not a neutral dark theme.
5. Buttons are always full pills (500pt radius) — never introduce a sharp-cornered rectangular button anywhere in the primary or secondary button set.
6. The active tab state is icon fill plus label color change only — never add a background tint pill behind the active tab icon.
7. Keep every currency figure tabular (`.monospacedDigit()`) — the NuConta balance and invoice total are the headline numbers of their tiles and must align cleanly.
8. Do not desaturate the purple or the product-accent colors in dark mode — only chrome (dividers, secondary text) should dim; the Roxinho card and brand purple stay fully vivid.
9. Keep copy friendly and jargon-free in tone (matching the source's Portuguese-first, conversational voice) even when localizing — the reassuring tone is as much a brand signal as the color.
</house_rules>
